name: Mal de Débarquement Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Mal de Débarquement Syndrome Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Persistent sensation of rocking, swaying, or bobbing motion following exposure to passive motion (e.g., boat, plane, or car travel)
Temporary symptom relief or reduction during passive motion (e.g., driving or riding in a vehicle)
Symptoms persisting for more than 48 hours after cessation of passive motion exposure
Exclusion of other vestibular, neurological, or psychiatric disorders that could explain symptoms
Presence of associated symptoms such as cognitive difficulties, headache, or visual motion sensitivity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria must be met, including persistent motion sensation after passive motion exposure, symptom relief with motion, symptom duration over 48 hours, and exclusion of other causes.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and often requires exclusion of other vestibular and neurological disorders.

imaging: Typically normal brain MRI and vestibular imaging studies
other: Vestibular function tests usually normal or nonspecific
Symptom improvement during passive motion is a key clinical feature

distinguishingFeatures: Episodic vertigo with headache and migraine features
Symptoms not consistently relieved by passive motion
Symptoms worsened by motion and visual stimuli but no relief during passive motion
Brief episodes of vertigo triggered by head position changes

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe vertigo with neurological deficits
Progressive neurological symptoms or focal signs
New onset hearing loss or severe tinnitus
references: Brown JJ, Baloh RW. Mal de Débarquement. Neurol Clin. 2017;35(3):725-735.
Cha YH. Mal de Débarquement Syndrome: A Review. Neurotherapeutics. 2016;13(3):447-455.
